extracted.intended_audience: Korean patent examiners, patent applicants and agents (KIPO context)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on handling international applications, amendment scope, and detailed procedures and requirements for issuing Notices of Grounds for Rejection (including timing, content, exceptions, and when rejection may be made without additional notice) under the Korean Patent Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Korean translation of PCT written amendments treated as voluntary amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: Where Korean translation of the written amendment regarding the description or claims pursuant to Articles 19 and 34 of the Patent Cooperation Treaty is submitted within the reference date, an examiner proceeds the examination procedure with considering an international application to have been voluntary-amended according to Article 47 of the Patent Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An examiner may request an applicant of an international application to submit copies of documents cited in the International Search Report or International Preliminary Examination Report; if considered necessary, the examiner (under the name of the Commissioner of KIPO) may request submission within a designated period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enlarged concept of novelty for international applications (pre-2015 filing-date rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where another application and the concerned application were all filed before December 31, 2014 (or another application filed before Dec 31, 2014 but concerned filed after Jan 1, 2015): an international application filed in a foreign language relied upon as 'another application' is considered to be laid open at the time of international publication; the scope of inventions of the 'another application' is limited to the inventions described in the specification, claims or drawings of both the international application as of the international filing date and its translation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where an international application claiming domestic priority is filed in a foreign language, the scope of inventions of the prior-filed application considered laid open or registered is limited to inventions described in the original specification or drawings of the prior-filed application that form the basis of the priority claim, out of inventions described both in the international application and its translation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enlarged concept of novelty for international applications (post-2015 filing-date rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where another application and the concerned application were all filed after January 1, 2015: an international application filed in a foreign language is considered laid open at time of international publication, but the scope of inventions of the 'another application' is limited to the inventions described in the description, claims or drawings of the international application as filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where an international application claiming domestic priority is filed in a foreign language, the scope of inventions of the prior-filed application considered laid open is limited to inventions described in the original specification or drawings of the prior-filed application which form the basis of the priority claim, out of those submitted as of the filing date of the international application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawn international applications cannot serve as 'another application' for novelty
rubrics_metrics.description: An international patent application or international utility model registration application that has been deemed withdrawn because the patent applicant did not file a Korean translation of the description and claims within the specified period (Article 201(4)) cannot be 'another application' in applying the provision of enlarged concept of novelty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment scope for international applications filed before Dec 31, 2014
rubrics_metrics.description: The specification or drawings of an international application filed in a foreign language can be amended within the scope of the matters described in the translations of the specification, claims, or drawings (limited to description parts on drawings) of the international application as of the international filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment scope for international applications filed after Jan 1, 2015
rubrics_metrics.description: A specification or drawing(s) of an international patent application filed in foreign language can be amended within the scope of matters described in the original document as of the filing date of the international patent application or in its Korean translation; care should be taken in determining whether to dismiss an amendment or issue a notice of rejection in view of an addition of a new matter. [Article 208(3) of the Patent Act of Korea]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to guidance on 'A new matter of an original document and of a Korean translation' for assessing new matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to notify applicant of grounds for rejection before making a rejection decision
rubrics_metrics.description: The Patent Act (Article 62) stipulates that the examiner, before making a decision to reject an application, should notify an applicant of the grounds for rejection and give him/her an opportunity to submit a written argument within a designated period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provision is designed to prevent errors or mistakes by an examiner and to provide an opportunity for error correction under the First-to-File rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground for rejection: claimed invention not patentable under specified Articles
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a claimed invention is not patentable pursuant to Article 25, 29, 32, 36(1),(3) or 44 of the Patent Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground for rejection: applicant not entitled to obtain a patent
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an application is filed by a person not entitled to obtain a patent according to Article 33(1), or where a claimed invention is not patentable pursuant to the proviso of the same Article.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground for rejection: violation of treaty provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Where it violates the provisions of the Treaty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground for rejection: failure to satisfy procedural requirements (Article 42/45)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where requirements in Article 42(3)(i), (4), (8) or Article 45 are not satisfied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground for rejection: amendment out of scope (Article 47(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an amendment is out of the scope prescribed in Article 47(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground for rejection: divisional application filed out of scope (Article 52(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a divisional application is filed out of the scope prescribed in Article 52(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground for rejection: converted application filed out of scope (Article 53(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a converted application is filed out of the scope prescribed in Article 53(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Time period for submission of written argument
rubrics_metrics.description: The period designated for submission of the argument shall be within two months regardless of whether an applicant is overseas resident or not.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a written argument requires tests and results evaluations whose time consumption is recognized, an additional period required for the tests or results evaluations may be added. Note: the period designated by the Commissioner of KIPO for an amendment request under Article 46 is within one month.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notify all grounds discovered during examination (complete notice) except specified exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Except for special cases, all the grounds for rejection discovered during an examination stage shall be notified in a complete manner; an examiner shall notify grounds of rejection altogether which might be conflicting, to protect applicant's procedural interests and expedite examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There are exceptions where limited notice is appropriate (see listed exceptions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exception: lack of clarity -> limited notice without prior art search
rubrics_metrics.description: Where contents of a claimed invention cannot be comprehended due to lack of clarity in the description, an examiner shall notify only the ground for rejection in violations of Article 42(3), (4) without conducting prior art search or assessing patentability requirements regarding novelty and inventive step.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However if the lack of clarity is insignificant so understanding is possible, the examiner shall conduct prior art search and review requirements within his/her comprehension and then notify all grounds discovered together.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exception: certain decisive defects notified without patentability judgement
rubrics_metrics.description: Where it is certain that a claim has newly added matter, or where it is not certain whether there is a ground pursuant to Article 32 (e.g., contravene public order), or where it is clear that a claimed invention does not constitute a statutory subject matter or is not industrially applicable, an examiner shall notify those grounds for rejection without judging other requirements for patentability such as novelty or inventive step.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exception: unity of invention (Article 45) handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an application fails to satisfy the requirement for a single patent application pursuant to Article 45, an examiner shall conduct an examination on inventions which fall under the scope of a single group and notify the grounds if discovered; however, for efficiency an examiner may notify the violation of Article 45 before judging other requirements for patentability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice must cite relevant legal provisions and be claim-by-claim
rubrics_metrics.description: When notifying a ground for rejection, the examiner shall stipulate the relevant provisions of the Act or laws and, for two or more claims included, the grounds for rejections should be indicated on a claim-by-claim basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Details referred to in '5.4 Examination Method by Each Claim'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice drafting requirements and evidence identification
rubrics_metrics.description: The grounds for rejection shall be stated with definite, concise, normal sentences to help applicant's understanding. For prior art used in inventive step, rely on the minimum number of references necessary and identify the parts of the references used; where denying novelty/inventive step by public knowledge/practice, specifically state facts showing public knowledge or practice; where denying written description requirement, specify deficient parts and stipulate corresponding reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventive step rejection must describe difference from closest prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: When notifying rejection for lack of inventive step, an examiner shall clearly describe the difference between the invention recited in the claims and the closest prior art reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exception: the examiner may not need to describe the difference where lack of novelty and lack of inventive step are notified together — then follow novelty assessment method for the novelty part, and inventive step notice may rely on logic that a person skilled in the art could easily make the invention from the prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner may suggest division or conversion but must disclaim legal effect
rubrics_metrics.description: If considered necessary for applicant convenience and for expeditious/accurate examination, an examiner may suggest a division or conversion of an application in the notice of rejection grounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner shall indicate in the notice that the suggestion has no legal effects and decision to carry out division or conversion shall be made by the applicant's intention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of erroneous written notices
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the written notice of rejection grounds having been issued contains errors in writing, an examiner shall issue a correct notice of grounds for rejection again, regardless of whether an applicant submits a written argument.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions: (i) where an applicant is deemed to submit a written argument based on his/her correct understanding of errors; (ii) where applicant does not submit arguments and the errors are clerical and not influential for the examiner's decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of self-evident errors in the specification
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the specification contains a self-evident error in writing, an examiner shall notify the error as 'Considerations' if there are other grounds for rejection; if no other grounds, the examiner shall communicate with the applicant (e.g., by telephone) and may advise an applicant to voluntarily amend or amend ex officio.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The advice or guidance communicated shall be documented in the 'Applicant/Agent Personal Interview Report'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection without additional notice when previously-notified grounds substantially coincide
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an examiner finds it appropriate to maintain the rejection which have been notified with taking any amendments into consideration, he/she should make a decision to reject without an additional notice of other rejection grounds which exists but is not notified, provided the decision to reject substantially coincides with the previously-notified rejection grounds and the applicant was practically given an opportunity to submit arguments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substantial coincidence is evaluated by whether the applicant was practically given an opportunity to submit written arguments, not confined to expression or sentence matching.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions allowing decision to reject based on the same claim after amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: In principle, a decision to reject can be made where: (1) the concerned claim is to be rejected based on the same provision of the Patent Act on patentability, and (2) the concerned claim lacks novelty and inventive step over the same reference or the same combinations of the same references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: prior notice of lack of inventive step over reference 1; after amendment adding B that was described in description before amendment, if still lacking inventive step over reference 1, decision to reject can be made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision to reject based on other claims (identical or adding limitations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an amendment makes a claim identical (or substantially identical) to another previously-rejected claim, a decision to reject the amended claim can be made on the basis of the ground notified to the other claim. Where an amendment adds limitations of another claim but the amended claim still fails to overcome a ground notified to the other claim based on the same provision, a decision to reject can be made because an opportunity for submission of written arguments has been sufficiently provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a new combination of references is required to reject the amended claim, a new ground is necessitated and, depending on stage, a second office action should be made or refusal to enter the amendment and proceed with original claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination whether applicant had opportunity to submit written arguments
rubrics_metrics.description: When the examiner intends to make a decision to reject based on reasons different from the ground previously notified to the claim concerned, he should carefully review whether an opportunity for submission of written arguments has been supplied to the applicant before making a decision to reject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show erroneous changes of references or claim scope may necessitate issuing a non-final rejection instead of a decision to reject; if prior erroneous notice caused the need for a new combination of references, examiner should refuse to enter the amendment rather than making a decision to reject.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determining opportunity regarding deficiencies in description (indefiniteness changes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Even though a ground of rejection is identical, if a term or phrase found indefinite in the claim is changed by amendment (so applicant could not reasonably know to respond), an opportunity for submission of written arguments is not considered to have been substantially provided, and a decision to reject cannot be made without special circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only where the amended claim fails to overcome the previously-notified ground and the concerned claim language substantially coincides can a decision to reject be made. New claims created by amendment that did not have previously-notified grounds ordinarily require providing an opportunity to submit written arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of notice: non-final rejection vs final rejection necessitated by amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: Notices of grounds for rejection are classified into 'final rejection necessitated by the amendments made in response to the previously-issued rejection' and 'non-final rejection' (first-time or not final).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-final rejection may be issued regardless of voluntary amendments if issued for the first time; if unamended portion includes a ground for rejection, non-final rejection shall be issued; if a ground arises not due to amendments, non-final notice shall be issued.
